text.p: Chrysler Corp said Wednesday it is extending its national consumer incentives program, which offers cash allowances or reduced interest rate financing to buyers of certain 1996 and 1997 models.
For most models, the program is extended through July 7.
The automaker's previous incentive program was to have expired April 7.

Chrysler said the amounts of the cash allowances available under the program are unchanged for all vehicles except the 1997 Dodge Ram Wagon, which qualifies for a $1,500 allowance effective April 1, 1997, up from $1,000.

As an alternative to the cash allowances, lower annual percentage rate financing rates are available. The alternative available rate is 3.9 percent for loans with terms from one to 60 months for the purchase of 1996 and 1997 Dodge Neon, Plymouth Neon, Dodge Avenger, Chrysler Sebring Coupe, Eagle Talon, Chrysler Cirrus, Dodge Stratus and Plymouth Breeze models.
The alternative available rate is 4.9 percent for loans with terms from one to 60 months for the purchase of 1996 and 1997 Chrysler Concorde, Dodge Intrepid and Eagle Vision models.
Alternative available rates on other vehicles in the program are unchanged.
